turns.speaker: host
turns.text: In Los Cabos this year crews closed 25 illegal water connections.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Theft ran above 300 litres every second.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Two hidden sources alone fed 120 tanker trucks a day.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Only three in ten people in BCS still receive water without breaks.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The rest wait on trucks that may never come.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The senator wants prison terms up to ten years for taking the water.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert light makes every drop visible on the road south.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet the lines keep vanishing.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050. Today a deep dive on Security. What does safety mean when the water itself keeps disappearing?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México reports that Senator Susana Zatarain wants up to 10 years in prison for water theft.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Water theft.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The bill adds an article to the Federal Penal Code and amends the National Waters Law to punish unauthorised extraction, tampering with infrastructure, clandestine wells and illegal water sales. Los Cabos found 25 illegal connections this year. The theft runs above 300 litres per second. Conagua closed two hidden sources that fed about 120 tanker trucks a day.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Three in ten people in BCS still have steady water, according to INEGI.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: How does that feel for a family waiting on a truck?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: At the Sea of Cortez Forum in Los Cabos, Agustín Coppel asked for 3.5 percent annual growth over 20 years across the five states, triple the foreign investment from the current USD 4.1 billion, and more public money for roads, ports, airport use, education and security.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: He noted BCS grew only 2.1 percent a year for the last decade.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Bitácora BCS says the state congress wants to take over port management from the navy after new tariffs upset operators in Cabo San Lucas. The schedule appeared on 1 October, though nothing changes yet without federal approval.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Ports carry people and goods. Who watches the gates?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias adds that Zatarain sees sales down 25 to 35 percent over two years and at least 27 restaurants closed or paused, partly from the feeling of insecurity, weak promotion and deteriorating infrastructure. She wants tourism revenue put back into the sector.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A 17.8 percent rise in the visitor fee to 1,158 pesos is set for 2027. Does the road feel safer when the lights stay on?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Luz, the state budget proposal puts security among the top lines. HOY BCS notes the 28.3 billion peso package for 2027.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes, and own revenue is meant to climb to 14.6 percent. Yet the Los Cabos revenue law sent to congress shows a 9 percent drop, nearly 675 million pesos less.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That cooling real estate market cuts property and transfer taxes sharply. How does the security line hold when the city’s own funds shrink 20 percent?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Palabra BCS reports the state lending a Comondú plot to the National Guard for 30 years. The land itself becomes part of the security infrastructure.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. And the same committee donates buildings to health services. The thread runs through land decisions and budget priorities together.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Imagen Radio adds that hoteliers link a 14 percent drop in U.S. visitors partly to security perceptions. The economic effect circles back to the revenue the budget needs.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the hidden design is this loop: land for the Guard, revenue shortfalls from tourism and real estate, and the priority line that must still be met.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Here is the turn. The portal’s water-first scenario names aquifer security as the precondition before any further growth. The same logic may quietly shape every other security choice.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the desert teach a city when water itself is the first security line?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Did you know the National Guard infrastructure was announced for national deployment?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The source lists it as announced but notes no BCS barracks with a primary source. It is the only security metric the portal records.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the plan stays national.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. No local details surface yet. Picture a quiet desert road at dusk, the long line of trucks heading south, and no new station marked on the map for the peninsula.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does that leave for the peninsula?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A question the portal leaves open. The state holds 798,447 people and a constant-price GDP of 187,152 million pesos in 2024, yet the Guard detail remains at the national level only.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. The road south stays long.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal’s Visión for governance points to a clear risk.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Without instruments that bind growth to measured ceilings.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes. The current path wins by the inertia of permits. Governance shows an EWMA of 3.57 this week, direction plus 0.50.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. What does the aspiration ask instead?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Public decisions that treat POEL, PDU, PMDU, consultations and ANP ceilings as prior conditions, not paperwork after the fact.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the levers to reach it?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Close the marked gaps with evidence first. Keep consultation and delivery to Congress visible. Use the state’s constrained board reading as a permit criterion.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Toward 2050 the tendencia describes a polycentric system, not one coastal formula.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos under water and power stress. East Cape in tension with protected areas. Todos Santos and El Pescadero as the Pacific amenity spine. La Paz as service capital and water-energy node. Loreto as tourism-conservation anchor. Comondú as agricultural hub with more room. Northern Mulegé as thinly documented corridor with a remote generation tender.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The desert light still falls differently on each stretch of that long road south.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Each vocation keeps a distinct role. New tourism or residential growth only where water and energy show evidenced margin or non-DMA source, without pretending NOM-011 credit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would East Cape and Loreto need to hold the line?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Respect ANP and POEL ceilings before scaling hospitality. Comondú and the north can add production and energy, yet without emptying services or ANPs.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The watchlist holds one concrete item.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The federal bill on water theft, up to 10 years in prison, and closures of illegal connections in Los Cabos. The second CSL desal plant sits at 75 percent, 250 liters per second, completion 2027.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would it take for each vocation to keep its distinct role?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The senator wants up to 10 years in prison for water theft, and Los Cabos already found 25 illegal connections this year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the state is lending a plot in Comondú to the National Guard for 30 years.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It feels like the same thread.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. What does the desert teach a city about keeping what it needs?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Congress wants to transfer ASIPONA to the state, while Los Cabos faces a 9 percent revenue drop in 2027 and restaurant closures.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The 28.3 billion peso budget might hold the key.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The takeaway is that security grows when we treat water, land and budgets as shared foundations before trouble arrives.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Stay with us. More Radio BCS2050 after the music.
